note: Individual reviews only. Each listed issue was reviewed as False Positive in the authenticated Sonar UI, with a matching RESOLVED status verified in the archived exact-commit analysis. No rule is disabled.

issues.rationale: This canvas draws a procedural status avatar; it has no click, keyboard or focus interaction. The image role is appropriate for the drawing, not an override on an interactive control. W3C ACT examples explicitly use a canvas with role=img and aria-label. Replacing it with a static img would remove the existing procedural state and reduced-motion behavior.
evidence: KubiAvatar.test.tsx: image role, state-specific accessible label, no click or tab stop; animation lifecycle and reduced-motion tests

issues.rationale: A native img cannot render this canvas drawing. Canvas does not support alt; role=img with a meaningful aria-label supplies its image semantics and accessible name, matching W3C ACT canvas examples. No rule disabling or inaccessible conversion is justified.
evidence: KubiAvatar.test.tsx: non-interactive canvas with state-specific image label

issues.rationale: The native modal dialog's click handler implements only light dismissal outside its bounding rectangle, not activation of non-interactive content. In-dialog content clicks do not dismiss it. Native cancel handles Escape, and an explicitly labelled native Close button provides keyboard dismissal. Initial focus and focus restoration were verified in Chrome.
evidence: Footer.test.tsx: native modal state, content-click preservation, close, cancel, backdrop and focus-return tests
Chrome desktop 1920x855: Enter opens :modal; Close license receives initial focus; Escape and a real outside click dismiss; focus returns to License

issues.rationale: The outside-click dismissal already has equivalent native keyboard behavior through the dialog cancel event (Escape) and native Close button. Adding a second artificial key handler solely to satisfy a JSX heuristic would duplicate native dialog behavior. It is not a click-only control.
evidence: Footer.test.tsx: cancel/close and focus-return regression coverage
Chrome desktop: actual Escape dismissal and License trigger focus return verified
